Pattern consistency: safe_float in /Users/julianamacbook/triggarr/triggarr/web/validation.py:203 is the float counterpart of safe_int (validation.py:180). It has the same (value, default, minimum, maximum) signature and adds a math.isfinite check. This extends the existing helper family rather than adding a competing one. A float helper is justified because GeneralConfig.shutdown_drain_timeout is typed float and tests/test_web.py:748 round-trips 120.5. safe_int would truncate that value.
No dependency issues: the only new import is one more name from triggarr.web.validation, which routes.py already imported. No new import cycle and no new third-party package.

Not yet wired up (sequenced, not a defect): triggarr/search/scheduler.py:58-81 still sets the drain timeout once at startup from the TRIGGARR_SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_TIMEOUT environment variable and never reads GeneralConfig.shutdown_drain_timeout. This is only a problem if 75-03 slips or is dropped before release. The orchestrator should confirm 75-03 is done before any push or tag.

Bounds asymmetry (deliberate, so not a finding): max_consecutive_failures enforces the same bounds in the model (Field ge=1, le=100) and in the form (safe_int 1..100). shutdown_drain_timeout has only ge=1.0 and allow_inf_nan=False in the model, while the 3600.0 ceiling exists only in the form clamp. A value above 3600 set by editing the TOML file directly will pass validation. The comment at /Users/julianamacbook/triggarr/triggarr/models/config.py:135-138 says this is intended ('form clamp (3600.0) is the UI ceiling'), so it is the author's call.

The default 60.0 is now written in three places: the GeneralConfig Field default, the safe_float default at routes.py:550, and the env-var fallback in scheduler.py. Two of these copies (the model and the routes call site) follow how every other general setting is handled, so this is below the rule-of-three threshold for a refactor. Plan 75-03 will probably rework the scheduler copy anyway.
